A 43-year-old woman comes to the clinic with complaints of intermittent non-bloody diarrhea for two
months. Her history reveals a 6-month raw food diet for weight loss, anxiety treated with fluvoxamine,
and osteopenia. Her family history includes a mother with lactose intolerance and recent osteoporosis
diagnosis. She denies substance use and mentions returning from Uganda three months ago. Physical
examination reveals stable vitals (temperature 98.6°F, blood pressure 158/71 mmHg, pulse 77/min,
respirations 18/min, O2 saturation 98% on room air) and a newly discovered systolic ejection murmur,
most prominent at the left second intercostal space. Which complication is most commonly associated
with the underlying cause of her presentation? Answer Choices: (A) Decreased urinary 5-HIAA (B)
Decreased levels of chromogranin A (C) Niacin deficiency (D) Positive hydrogen breath test (E)
Elevated serum serotonin levels (F) Folate deficiency (G) Vitamin D deficiency (H) Vitamin B12
malabsorption (I) Thiamine deficiency (J) Iron deficiency anemia
 A. Iron deficiency anemia
B. Niacin deficiency
C. Thiamine deficiency

D. Vitamin B12 malabsorption
E. Positive hydrogen breath test
F. Decreased levels of chromogranin A
G. Folate deficiency
H. Elevated serum serotonin levels
I. Decreased urinary 5-HIAA
